item.title: Laya Healthcare customers face increased in cost of health insurance
item.description: Laya Healthcare customers are facing an increase in the cost of their health insurance, after the company announced its increasing the prices of 65 of its health insurance policies by an average of 4.7%. It's the equivalent increase of around 80 Euro per adult annually. The price hikes will take effect from the start of April. Dermot Goode of health insurance ireland.ie said the changes will be significant. Advertisement

item.title: Ballaghaderreen TD hits out at justice department for not funding new childcare centre
item.description: A Ballaghaderreen TD is hitting out at the Department of Justice for not funding the town's new childcare centre. The one-million-euro facility is being built in The Shambles, across the road from St Nathy's College. Work is nearly complete and it's on course to open by June. Sinn Féin TD Claire Kerrane says the Department of Justice should have funded it - given the amount of refugees in the town: Advertisement

item.title: Longford senator calls for raised pedestrian crossings outside schools
item.description: A Longford senator is calling for raised pedestrian crossings outside every school in Ireland. Paraic Brady says it's vital because a large amount of children are outside them. The Fine Gael senator says other safety improvements are also needed outside schools. He says traffic has slowed down hugely outside his local school recently - due to safety measures: Advertisement

item.title: Almost 20,000 across region enrolled in retirement savings system
item.description: There are almost 20,000 in the Shannonside region enrolled in the Government's retirement savings system. Figures were revealed earlier this week following a parliamentary question from Dublin South Central TD Catherine Ardagh to Minister for Social Protection, Dara Calleary. The Programme for Government contains a commitment to introduce the Automatic Enrolment Retirement Savings System. item.description: Follow live updates as Roscommon travel to Salthill to face Galway. Roscommon are second in division one after wins over Monaghan and Armagh. Whereas, Galway beat Armagh in round one, drew with Kerry and lost to Mayo. Throw-in is 7pm. Advertisement

item.title: Roscommon comeback to down Galway
item.description: Roscommon produced a remarkable second-half comeback to snatch a dramatic one-point victory over Galway in Salthill. Trailing by 11 points at the interval, the Rossies stormed back with the aid of a strong breeze to claim victory.
